title: P versus NP
open: Is P = NP? Equivalently, does every problem with efficiently verifiable solutions also have efficiently computable solutions?
status: Open since 1971 (Cook–Levin). Notorious as one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems (2000). All known techniques provably fail: relativization (Baker–Gill–Solovay 1975), natural proofs (Razborov–Rudich 1997), algebrization (Aaronson–Wigderson 2009).
why: The single most consequential question in computer science; separates feasible verification from feasible computation across all of mathematics and cryptography's foundations.
key_works: S. Cook, "The complexity of theorem-proving procedures", STOC 1971; L. Levin, "Universal sequential search problems", Problems of Information Transmission 1973; R. Razborov, S. Rudich, "Natural proofs", JCSS 1997 (DOI:10.1006/jcss.1997.1494); S. Aaronson, A. Wigderson, "Algebrization: a new barrier in complexity theory", TOCT 2009 (arXiv:0806.1347); Clay Mathematics Institute, "P vs NP Problem", claymath.org/millennium/p-vs-np

title: NP versus coNP
open: Is NP = coNP? Equivalently, do complements of NP problems have short certificates?
status: Open since the 1970s; believed false. Implies P ≠ NP if separated. No oracle with insight; duality phenomena (LP, semidefinite) show partial worlds where it holds.
why: Separation would rule out short proofs of unsatisfiability (SAT refutations), bounding proof systems and many verification tasks.
key_works: S. Cook, "The complexity of theorem-proving procedures", STOC 1971; S. Arora, B. Barak, "Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach", Cambridge 2009, ch. 3-5

title: One-way functions existence
open: Do one-way functions exist? Equivalently (by Impagliazzo), is P = NP ∩ coNP enough to kill them — do easy average-case hard problems exist?
status: Open; existence implies P ≠ NP (but not conversely). Impagliazzo's five worlds (1995) frame the possibilities.
why: One-way functions are necessary and sufficient for much of modern cryptography; their existence is the minimal complexity assumption for private-key crypto.
key_works: R. Impagliazzo, "A personal view of average-case complexity", CCC 1995; O. Goldreich, "Foundations of Cryptography vol. 1", Cambridge 2001

title: BPP versus P (derandomization)
open: Can every randomized polynomial-time algorithm be derandomized, i.e., BPP = P?
status: Widely believed; equivalent to building sufficiently strong pseudorandom generators from hard functions. Impagliazzo–Wigderson (1997) shows BPP=P if E requires 2^Ω(n) circuits. Full derandomization needs circuit lower bounds that are themselves open.
why: Determines whether randomness is ever essential for efficient computation; underpins PRG constructions used throughout derandomization and crypto.
key_works: R. Impagliazzo, A. Wigderson, "P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits", STOC 1997 (DOI:10.1145/258533.258590); N. Nisan, A. Wigderson, "Hardness vs randomness", JCSS 1994

title: Circuit lower bounds for NEXP
open: Prove NEXP ⊄ P/poly (NEXP has no polynomial-size circuits). Even MA_EXP ⊄ P/poly is open in the non-uniform setting.
status: Best known: Williams (2010) proved NEXP ⊄ ACC0. The general P/poly bound resists all known techniques; natural proofs barrier applies to much stronger targets.
why: The front line of lower bounds; any superpolynomial circuit lower bound for NEXP would be the first "real" lower bound beyond ACC0 and would unlock a path toward P vs NP.
key_works: R. Williams, "Nonuniform ACC circuit lower bounds", JACM 2014 (arXiv:0907.4753); E. Allender et al. on barriers; R. Ryan Williams survey "Some Estimated Likelihoods for Computational Complexity" (arXiv:1502.07816) (verify)

title: Natural proofs barrier scope
open: Find lower-bound techniques that evade natural proofs — e.g., prove lower bounds for functions that are not "constructively hard" against subexponential-size circuit classes.
status: Open since Razborov–Rudich (1997). Known escape routes: arithmetization/algebrization (limited), diagonalization against oracles, and Williams' algorithmic method — each only partially effective.
why: Tells us WHY lower bounds are stuck; any new proof must either defeat the barrier or exploit non-natural predicates.
key_works: R. Razborov, S. Rudich, "Natural proofs", JCSS 1997; S. Aaronson, A. Wigderson, "Algebrization", TOCT 2009

title: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH)
open: Is solving k-SAT with n variables and unbounded k essentially 2^n time, i.e., does the SETH constant s_inf = lim s_k equal 1?
status: Open since 1999 (Impagliazzo–Paturi). Known: sparsification lemma reduces dense-to-sparse instances; SETH implies lower bounds for dozens of problems (drag reductions of n^(2-ε) for Edit Distance, etc.).
why: The load-bearing assumption of fine-grained complexity; its failure would collapse a web of conditional lower bounds.
key_works: R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, "On the complexity of k-SAT", JCSS 2001; ETH chapter in "Fine-Grained Complexity" course notes by V. Williams (verify)

title: Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH)
open: Is 3-SAT not solvable in 2^{o(n)} time?
status: Open since 1999; implied by SETH. Contrasts with subexponential algorithms known for restricted formulas (Schöning 1999).
why: Underlies the (no subexponential algorithms for NP-hard problems) view; base of many reductions in parameterized complexity.
key_works: R. Impagliazzo, R. Paturi, "On the complexity of k-SAT", JCSS 2001

title: 3SUM conjecture
open: Is there a truly subquadratic (O(n^{2-ε})) algorithm for deciding whether n integers contain three summing to zero?
status: Open since Gajentaan–Overmars (1995) popularized it. Best known: slightly subquadratic n^2/polylog (Baran–Demaine–Pătraşcu 2008; then n^2 (log log n)^{O(1)} / log^Ω(1) n by Chan 2018); near-linear quantum algorithm (Ambainis 2007).
why: Anchors quadratic lower bounds for dozens of geometry and string problems; a rare unconditional "hard core" candidate.
key_works: A. Gajentaan, M. Overmars, "On a class of O(n^2) problems in computational geometry", CGTA 1995; T. Chan, "More logarithmic-factor speedups for 3SUM, (median,+)-convolution, and some geometric 3SUM-hard problems", SODA 2018 (arXiv:1708.03063)

title: APSP subcubic barrier
open: Is there a truly subcubic (n^{3-ε}) algorithm for All-Pairs Shortest Paths in weighted graphs?
status: Open for decades. Best known ~n^3 / 2^{Ω(sqrt log n)} by Williams (2014) building on Chan; equivalent subcubic-hard class (Vassilevska Williams–Williams 2010: APSP, negative triangle, etc. all subcubic-equivalent).
why: Central to the fine-grained web; many graph problems are subcubically equivalent to it.
key_works: V. Vassilevska Williams, R. Williams, "Subcubic equivalences between path, matrix and triangle problems", FOCS 2010 (arXiv:1011.4901); R. Williams, "Faster all-pairs shortest paths via circuit complexity", STOC 2014 (arXiv:1312.6680)

title: Orthogonal Vectors conjecture
open: Is there an O(n^{2-ε}) algorithm for deciding whether two lists of n boolean vectors of dimension d = polylog n contain an orthogonal pair?
status: Open; equivalent to SETH-hardness of many quadratic problems (with Abboud–Henzinger–Vassilevska Williams). Hashing heuristics solve random instances fast.
why: OV is the cleanest known consequence of SETH; reducing OV to 3SUM-style problems is the main technique in conditional lower bound proofs.
key_works: A. Abboud, T. Henzinger, V. Vassilevska Williams, "Popular conjectures imply strong hard-ness for dynamic and integer programming", FOCS 2015 (arXiv:1502.06023)

title: Matrix multiplication exponent ω
open: What is ω, the infimum exponent such that n×n matrices multiply in n^{ω+ε} time? Is ω = 2?
status: Open since Strassen (1969, ω ≤ 2.81). Current record: ω < 2.371866 (Duan–Wu–Zhou 2025, improving Alman–Vassilevska Williams 2021's 2.3728596). Group-theoretic approaches (Cohn–Umans) stalled at same barriers.
why: Fast matrix multiplication is a subroutine in nearly all of numerical algebra; the value of ω sets limits across combinatorial and scientific computing.
key_works: V. Strassen, "Gaussian elimination is not optimal", Numer. Math. 1969; J. Alman, V. Vassilevska Williams, "A refined laser method and faster matrix multiplication", SODA 2021 (arXiv:2010.05846); R. Duan, H. Wu, R. Zhou, "Faster matrix multiplication via asymmetric hashing", FOCS 2025 (verify)

title: Integer factorization complexity
open: Can integers be factored in polynomial time (classically)? Can it be done substantially faster than subexponential L_N[1/3] number-field-sieve time?
status: Open. Best classical: NFS at exp((~1.9)(ln N)^{1/3}(ln ln N)^{2/3}); quantum: Shor's algorithm is polynomial (1994). No classical poly algorithm despite decades; not even known NP-hard (and believed outside P but in NP ∩ coNP).
why: RSA's security rests on factoring hardness; a classical poly algorithm breaks most deployed public-key crypto.
key_works: P. Shor, "Algorithms for quantum computation: discrete logarithms and factoring", FOCS 1994; A. Lenstra et al., "The number field sieve", 1993

title: Graph isomorphism complexity
status: Open. Best: quasipolynomial time n^{polylog n} (Babai 2016, with Helfgott's simplification). Not believed NP-complete (would collapse PH by Boppana–Håstad–Zachos). Practical solvers (nauty, Traces) handle huge instances.
why: GI is the canonical "NP-intermediate" candidate; its orbit-closure structure connects to group theory and practical isomorphism testing (chemistry, circuits).
key_works: L. Babai, "Graph isomorphism in quasipolynomial time", STOC 2016 (arXiv:1512.03547); J. Köbler, U. Schöning, J. Torán, "The Graph Isomorphism Problem: Its Structural Complexity", Birkhäuser 1993

title: Unique Games Conjecture
open: Is the Unique Games Conjecture true? (Constant-gap unique-label-cover is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable vs (1-ε)-satisfiable.)
status: Open since Khot (2002). Supports optimal inapproximability for Vertex Cover, MaxCut (via Goemans–Williamson matching), and broad integrality-gap phenomena. Subexponential algorithms for restricted graphs (Arora–Barak–Steurer 2010) weakened some forms; recent algorithmic progress on 2-to-2 games (Khot–Minzer–Safra 2023 structure theorem) suggests a nuanced truth.
why: If true, yields a sweeping theory of hardness of approximation matching SDP algorithms; if false, the entire hardness-of-approximation edifice needs rework.
key_works: S. Khot, "On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games", STOC 2002; S. Khot, D. Minzer, M. Safra, "Pseudorandom structure in 2-to-2 games", Annals of Mathematics 2023 (arXiv:1803.03186)

title: Optimal PCP length
open: How small can a probabilistically checkable proof be? Can the verification query length and proof length both be made optimal (constant queries, near-linear length)?
status: Open. Dinur's PCP (2007) gives constant-query, polynomial-length via gap amplification; short PCPs of near-linear length exist (Dinur–Harsha 2013) with worse parameters. The tradeoff frontier (query vs length vs alphabet) is actively open.
why: PCP parameters control inapproximability reductions; tight PCPs would settle hardness-of-approximation constants.
key_works: I. Dinur, "The PCP theorem by gap amplification", JACM 2007; I. Dinur, P. Harsha, "Composition of low-error 2-query PCPs using decodable PCPs", SIAM J. Computing 2013 (arXiv:1206.6432)

title: Frege system lower bounds
open: Prove superpolynomial lower bounds on proof length in Frege systems (and stronger: bounded-depth Frege, Extended Frege) for any natural tautology family.
status: Open. No superpolynomial Frege lower bound known for any explicit tautology; resolution is well understood (Haken 1985 for pigeonhole; for all tautologies by Chvátal–Szemerédi).
why: Bounds SAT-solver power in the idealized limit; EF lower bounds would imply major circuit lower bounds (P/poly separations).
key_works: A. Haken, "The intractability of resolution", TCS 1985; P. Beame, T. Pitassi, "Propositional proof complexity: past, present, and future", Bull. EATCS 1998

title: Dynamic connectivity lower bound
open: Can dynamic graph connectivity (edge insert/delete, connectivity queries) be maintained faster than polylog amortized? Is there a matching cell-probe lower bound separating it from dynamic trees?
status: Open. Upper: O(log^2 n) deterministic (Holm–de Lichtenberg–Thorup 2001), improved randomized O(log n (log log n)^2) (Wulff-Nilsen 2023, verify). Cell-probe lower bounds: Ω(log n) (Patrascu–Demaine 2006 for partial sums implies barriers), but tight bounds remain open.
why: The flagship dynamic data structure problem; its exact complexity gates a family of dynamic graph algorithms (MST, subgraph connectivity).
key_works: J. Holm, K. de Lichtenberg, M. Thorup, "Poly-logarithmic deterministic fully-dynamic algorithms for connectivity, minimum spanning tree, 2-edge, and biconnectivity", JACM 2001; M. Pătraşcu, E. Demaine, "Logarithmic lower bounds in the cell-probe model", SIAM J. Computing 2006 (arXiv:cs/0502041)

title: Cell-probe lower bounds for static data structures
open: Prove t_q = Ω(log^2 n / log w) type optimal lower bounds for natural static problems (3SUM indexing, adjacency in nnz o(n^2) graphs, predecessor) in the cell-probe model with polynomial space.
status: Open; best lower bounds for predecessor are Ω(log n / log(w/n)) (Pătraşcu–Thorup 2006) matching van Emde Boas-type upper bounds, but for many listing/reporting problems only log^Ω(1) bounds exist. Larsen's cell-sampling technique gives Ω(log^2 n / log(Sw/n)) for some range problems (2012).
why: A t_q lower bound beyond log^2 n for any explicit problem would be a breakthrough comparable to circuit lower bounds.
key_works: K. Green Larsen, "The cell probe complexity of dynamic range counting", STOC 2012 (arXiv:1203.5135); M. Pătraşcu, M. Thorup, "Time-space trade-offs for predecessor search", STOC 2006

title: Competitive ratio lower bound for online algorithms
open: Determine the exact competitive ratio of online algorithms for core problems like k-server (is the randomized competitive ratio O(log k)?), online paging, and metrical task systems.
status: Open. k-server deterministic ratio conjectured k (proved on special metrics: trees, and via Bansal et al. quasi-poly randomized poly-log bounds); the "randomized k-server conjecture" O(log k) remains open.
why: These are the cleanest models of decision-making under uncertainty; exact ratios characterize the cost of irrevocability.
key_works: Y. Bartal et al., "Competitive analysis of the k-server problem", 1990s surveys; N. Bansal et al., "A polylog competitive algorithm for metrical task systems", SODA 2023 (verify)

title: MCSP complexity
open: What is the complexity of the Minimum Circuit Size Problem (given a truth table, does it have a circuit of size s)? Is MCSP NP-complete?
status: Open since the 1950s (Kolmogorov). Known: in NP, not known complete; hardness under plausible reductions to many problems; strong connections to one-way functions and learning (Carmosino–Impagliazzo–Kabanets–Kolokolova 2016).
why: Meta-complexity is currently the most promising lens on P vs NP; MCSP sits at its center, connecting circuit complexity, learning, and crypto.
key_works: E. Allender, "The new complexity landscape around circuit minimization", Current Trends in TCS 2021 (arXiv:2010.10613); I. Carmosino, R. Impagliazzo, V. Kabanets, A. Kolokolova, "Learning algorithms from natural proofs", CCC 2016 (arXiv:1601.01272)

title: Average-case complexity theory
open: Build a robust theory of average-case NP hardness: natural distributional problems complete for DistNP under realistic reductions.
status: Open since Levin (1986). Known: if one-way functions exist then DistNP has hard problems (Impagliazzo–Levin 1990: random self-reducibility arguments), but no natural complete problem is known without assumptions.
why: Worst-case hardness may not reflect real-world intractability; average-case understanding is what cryptography and heuristics actually need.
key_works: L. Levin, "Average case complete problems", SIAM J. Computing 1986; R. Impagliazzo, L. Levin, "No better ways to generate hard NP instances than picking uniformly at random", FOCS 1990

title: P versus PSPACE
open: Prove or refute that every polynomial-space computation can be performed in polynomial time.
status: Open since the 1970s. Time- and space-hierarchy theorems separate other resource levels but do not separate P from PSPACE.
why: Determines whether polynomially bounded memory can support fundamentally more computation than polynomially bounded time.
key_works: Stockmeyer and Meyer (1973), *Word Problems Requiring Exponential Time*; Arora and Barak (2009), *Computational Complexity*.

s2_matches.title: NP versus PSPACE

title: L versus NL
open: Determine whether directed graph reachability can be decided deterministically using \(O(\log n)\) workspace.
status: Open since the 1960s–1970s. Savitch gives deterministic \(O(\log^2 n)\) space; Reingold solved undirected connectivity in logarithmic space, not directed reachability.
why: Would identify the value of nondeterminism under severe memory constraints.
key_works: Savitch (1970), *Relationships between Nondeterministic and Deterministic Tape Complexities*, DOI: 10.1016/S0022-0000(70)80006-X; Reingold (2008), *Undirected Connectivity in Log-Space*, DOI: 10.1145/1391289.1391291.

title: P versus uniform NC
open: Determine whether every polynomial-time computation admits polynomial-size, polylogarithmic-depth uniform Boolean circuits.
status: Open since the development of P-completeness and parallel complexity. Numerous natural problems are P-complete, but their presumed inherent sequentiality remains conditional.
why: Separates problems that parallel hardware can accelerate dramatically from genuinely sequential computations.
key_works: Ladner (1975), *The Circuit Value Problem Is Log Space Complete for P*; Greenlaw, Hoover, and Ruzzo (1995), *Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory*; Arora–Barak textbook.

title: Uniform NC¹ versus L
open: Determine whether every deterministic logarithmic-space computation has logarithmic-depth, polynomial-size, bounded-fan-in uniform circuits.
status: Open for decades. Barrington’s theorem characterizes nonuniform NC¹ using constant-width branching programs, but does not collapse logarithmic-space computation to NC¹.
why: Identifies whether long, memory-efficient computations can always be compressed into very shallow parallel computations.
key_works: Barrington (1989), *Bounded-Width Polynomial-Size Branching Programs Recognize Exactly Those Languages in NC¹*; Arora and Barak (2009), *Computational Complexity*.

title: Infinitude of the polynomial hierarchy
open: Prove that \(\Sigma_k^P\ne\Sigma_{k+1}^P\) for every fixed \(k\), or establish a collapse.
status: Open since Stockmeyer’s 1976 formulation. Oracle worlds exhibit both collapses and infinite hierarchies, demonstrating limits of relativizing arguments.
why: Determines whether each additional alternation of existential and universal certification increases computational power.
key_works: Stockmeyer (1976), *The Polynomial-Time Hierarchy*, DOI: 10.1016/0304-3975(76)90061-X; Baker, Gill, and Solovay (1975), *Relativizations of the P =? NP Question*.

title: NP versus polynomial-size circuits
open: Prove that some language in NP requires superpolynomial-size unrestricted Boolean circuits; equivalently, prove \(\mathrm{NP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\).
status: Open since the 1970s. Karp–Lipton shows that containment would collapse the polynomial hierarchy, but this consequence is not a contradiction.
why: Rules out even nonuniform, input-length-specific efficient solutions to all NP problems.
key_works: Karp and Lipton (1980), *Some Connections Between Nonuniform and Uniform Complexity Classes*; Razborov and Rudich (1997), *Natural Proofs*; Viola (2017), *Selected Challenges in Computational Lower Bounds*.

title: Graph isomorphism in polynomial time
open: Give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm deciding whether two arbitrary finite graphs are isomorphic.
status: Studied for more than five decades. Babai’s quasipolynomial-time algorithm is a major general breakthrough; polynomial time remains unresolved.
why: Would settle a central natural problem not known to be either NP-complete or polynomial-time solvable.
key_works: Babai (2016), *Graph Isomorphism in Quasipolynomial Time*, arXiv:1512.03547, DOI: 10.1145/2897518.2897542.

title: Berman–Hartmanis isomorphism conjecture
open: Determine whether every pair of NP-complete languages under polynomial-time many-one reductions is related by a polynomial-time computable bijection whose inverse is also polynomial-time computable.
status: Proposed in 1977. Large families of natural complete sets satisfy the conjectured structure; a general proof or counterexample is unknown.
why: Asks whether NP-complete problems are fundamentally the same object up to efficient relabeling.
key_works: Berman and Hartmanis (1977), *On Isomorphisms and Density of NP and Other Complete Sets*, DOI: 10.1137/0206023.

title: NP versus UP
open: Determine whether every NP language has an unambiguous polynomial-time verifier: at most one accepting witness for each input.
status: Open since the 1970s. Valiant–Vazirani provides randomized isolation into unique-solution promise problems, not an unconditional equality of NP and UP.
why: Clarifies whether ambiguity is an essential source of computational difficulty.
key_works: Valiant and Vazirani (1986), *NP Is as Easy as Detecting Unique Solutions*, DOI: 10.1016/0304-3975(86)90135-0.

title: Complete problems for NP ∩ coNP
open: Determine whether \(\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}\) has a complete language under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions.
status: A longstanding structural question. Natural members do not supply a known complete representative, and oracle results show that standard relativizing approaches face obstacles.
why: Determines whether the class of problems with short certificates on both sides has a universal hardest problem.
key_works: Dose (2019), *P-Optimal Proof Systems for Each NP-Set but No Complete Disjoint NP-Pairs Relative to an Oracle*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2019.47.

title: Superlinear unrestricted Boolean circuit lower bounds
open: Exhibit an explicit polynomial-time computable Boolean function requiring \(\omega(n)\) gates in unrestricted bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits.
status: Open for decades despite strong bounds for restricted models. Counting proves that most functions require exponentially many gates, but does not make them efficiently explicit.
why: Would cross a basic barrier toward general circuit lower bounds.
key_works: Shannon (1949), *The Synthesis of Two-Terminal Switching Circuits*; Viola (2017), *Selected Challenges in Computational Lower Bounds*.

title: Superpolynomial general formula lower bounds
open: Find an explicit function in P requiring superpolynomial-size unrestricted Boolean formulas.
status: Open for decades. Strong polynomial lower bounds and exponential bounds for restricted formula models are known, but unrestricted superpolynomial bounds remain elusive.
why: Would prove that reusing intermediate computations can provide more than a polynomial advantage.
key_works: Håstad (1998), *The Shrinkage Exponent of de Morgan Formulas Is 2*; Hoza (2024), circuit-complexity course materials.

title: NP outside ACC⁰
open: Prove that NP is not contained in polynomial-size constant-depth circuits with AND, OR, NOT, and modular counting gates.
status: Williams established that NEXP is not contained in ACC⁰. Moving the hard language down to NP remains unresolved.
why: Would substantially strengthen the algorithm-to-lower-bound approach in a model beyond ordinary AC⁰.
key_works: Williams (2011), *Non-uniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds*; Hoza (2024), circuit-complexity materials.

title: Majority outside ACC⁰
open: Prove that majority cannot be computed by polynomial-size ACC⁰ circuits, allowing any fixed modulus and fixed depth.
status: Majority is outside AC⁰, but its separation from ACC⁰ remains unresolved. This is a concrete function-specific target rather than a class-separation formulation.
why: Would separate approximate counting power from constant-depth modular computation.
key_works: Razborov and Smolensky’s 1980s modular-circuit lower bounds; Williams (2011), *Non-uniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds*; Hoza’s course.

title: Superpolynomial depth-two threshold lower bounds
open: Give an explicit polynomial-time computable function requiring superpolynomially many gates in a threshold-of-threshold circuit, \(\mathrm{THR}\circ\mathrm{THR}\).
status: Open despite substantial lower bounds for restricted threshold architectures and stronger depth restrictions. General polynomial-size depth-two threshold circuits remain poorly understood.
why: Establishes limitations of a simple but expressive neural-style architecture.
key_works: Hajnal, Maass, Pudlák, Szegedy, and Turán (1993), *Threshold Circuits of Bounded Depth*; Viola (2017), lower-bound challenges.

title: Valiant’s explicit matrix rigidity problem
open: Construct an explicit family of \(n\times n\) matrices over a specified fixed field with rigidity \(R_A(\varepsilon n)\ge n^{1+\delta}\) for constants \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\).
status: Proposed in 1977. Random matrices are highly rigid; achieving the needed parameters explicitly remains open, and several once-promising structured matrices have turned out insufficiently rigid.
why: Strong explicit rigidity would yield lower bounds for important classes of linear circuits.
key_works: Valiant (1977), *Graph-Theoretic Arguments in Low-Level Complexity*; Ramya (2020), *Recent Progress on Matrix Rigidity—A Survey*, arXiv:2009.09460.

title: Superlinear explicit XOR-circuit lower bounds
open: Construct an explicit binary matrix whose linear transformation requires \(\omega(n)\) two-input XOR gates.
status: Counting gives large lower bounds for most matrices, but explicit unrestricted linear-circuit lower bounds remain weak. Cancellation-free and other restricted models are better understood.
why: Would establish unavoidable cost for explicit linear transforms used in computation and communication.
key_works: Valiant (1977), *Graph-Theoretic Arguments in Low-Level Complexity*; Ramya’s rigidity survey and associated bibliography.

title: VP versus VNP
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Determine whether every polynomial family in VNP has polynomial-size arithmetic circuits; over characteristic zero, separating the permanent from VP would suffice.
status: Valiant introduced the classes in 1979. Restricted circuit lower bounds are extensive, but the general separation remains open.
why: This is the central algebraic analogue of efficient computation versus efficient exponential summation.
key_works: Valiant (1979), *Completeness Classes in Algebra*; Shpilka and Yehudayoff (2010), *Arithmetic Circuits: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Questions*, DOI: 10.1561/0400000039.

title: Arithmetic circuits versus branching programs
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Determine whether every polynomial-size, polynomial-degree arithmetic circuit can be simulated by a polynomial-size algebraic branching program: VP = VBP.
status: Open for decades. Quasipolynomial simulations and strong results for restricted models do not establish polynomial equivalence.
why: Measures the computational value of general arithmetic circuit structure beyond iterated linear-algebraic computation.
key_works: Valiant, Skyum, Berkowitz, and Rackoff (1983), *Fast Parallel Computation of Polynomials Using Few Processors*; Shpilka–Yehudayoff survey.

title: Arithmetic formulas versus branching programs
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Prove or refute that polynomial-size arithmetic formulas and polynomial-size algebraic branching programs compute the same polynomial families.
status: Open in the unrestricted commutative setting. Formula lower bounds for determinant or iterated matrix multiplication strong enough to separate these classes remain unavailable.
why: Determines how much benefit arithmetic computation obtains from sharing subcomputations along different paths.
key_works: Valiant et al. (1983), *Fast Parallel Computation of Polynomials Using Few Processors*; Shpilka–Yehudayoff (2010).

title: Superpolynomial determinantal complexity of the permanent
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Prove that expressing the \(n\times n\) permanent as the determinant of a matrix of affine-linear forms requires superpolynomial matrix dimension.
status: Open since Valiant’s work. Quadratic-scale lower bounds are known; a 2026 Kumar–Volk preprint develops further quadratic lower-bound results, still far from superpolynomial growth.
why: A concrete route toward separating algebraic complexity classes.
key_works: Mignon and Ressayre (2004), *A Quadratic Bound for the Determinant and Permanent Problem*; Kumar and Volk (2026), *A Quadratic Lower Bound on Determinantal Complexity*, ECCC TR26-218.

title: Deterministic polynomial-time white-box PIT
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Given an arithmetic circuit of polynomially bounded degree over a specified effective field, decide deterministically in polynomial time whether it computes the zero polynomial.
status: Randomized polynomial-time identity testing has been available for decades. General deterministic polynomial-time testing remains open despite many restricted-model algorithms.
why: Would derandomize a fundamental primitive in symbolic algebra and imply significant circuit lower bounds through known connections.
key_works: Schwartz (1980); Zippel (1979); Kabanets and Impagliazzo (2004), *Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds*; Hu, van Melkebeek, and Morgan (2024), DOI: 10.4086/toc.2024.v020a001.

title: Polynomial-size explicit hitting sets for general circuits
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Construct polynomial-size hitting sets, computable in polynomial time, for all arithmetic circuits of size \(s\) and degree polynomial in \(s\).
status: Open in the general model. This asks for black-box derandomization, a stronger access restriction than white-box PIT.
why: Would allow deterministic verification when a polynomial computation is available only through evaluations.
key_works: Heintz and Schnorr (1980), *Testing Polynomials Which Are Easy to Compute*; Shpilka–Yehudayoff (2010); Hu–van Melkebeek–Morgan (2024).

bib.title: Polynomial-size explicit hitting sets for general circuits

title: Matrix multiplication exponent two
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Prove \(\omega=2\): for every \(\varepsilon>0\), multiply two \(n\times n\) matrices using \(O(n^{2+\varepsilon})\) arithmetic operations.
status: Open since Strassen’s 1969 breakthrough. A verified 2025 benchmark is \(\omega<2.371339\); the lower bound remains 2.
why: Would accelerate a large family of algebraic, graph, and scientific computations.
key_works: Strassen (1969), *Gaussian Elimination Is Not Optimal*; Alman et al. (2025), *More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication*, DOI: 10.1137/1.9781611978322.63.

s2_matches.title: Ubiquity of the exponent of matrix multiplication

title: Shub–Smale integer-root τ conjecture
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Prove that a nonzero integer polynomial computed by a constant-free arithmetic straight-line program of length \(\tau\) has at most \((\tau+1)^C\) integer roots for some universal constant \(C\).
status: Proposed in the 1990s. General polynomial root-count bounds in terms of straight-line complexity remain unavailable.
why: Links arithmetic computation to Diophantine complexity and major algebraic lower-bound questions.
key_works: Shub and Smale (1995), *On the Intractability of Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz and an Algebraic Version of NP ≠ P*; Bürgisser’s work connecting τ-type conjectures to complexity.

title: Real τ conjecture for sums of products of sparse polynomials
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Bound the number of distinct real roots of a nonzero polynomial \(P=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\prod_{j=1}^{m} f_{ij}\), with each \(f_{ij}\) having at most \(t\) monomials, by a polynomial in \(k,m,t\).
status: Open in this structured model. Average-case versions are known; the analogous claim for arbitrary arithmetic circuits is false and is not the problem listed here.
why: Would connect fewnomial geometry to arithmetic lower bounds.
key_works: Hrubeš (2013), *On the Real τ-Conjecture and the Distribution of Complex Roots*; Briquel and Bürgisser, *The Real Tau-Conjecture Is True on Average*, arXiv:1806.00417.

bib.title: Real τ conjecture for sums of products of sparse polynomials

title: Deterministic PIT for general noncommutative circuits
subfield: Algebraic complexity and polynomial identity testing
open: Give deterministic polynomial-time identity testing for general noncommutative arithmetic circuits with polynomially bounded syntactic degree.
status: Raz–Shpilka solved important formula and branching-program cases in 2005. General circuits with sharing remain a different, unresolved problem.
why: Would advance symbolic computation in free algebras and clarify the power of circuit reuse.
key_works: Raz and Shpilka (2005), *Deterministic Polynomial Identity Testing in Non-Commutative Models*; Li, Tzameret, and Wang (2015), *Non-Commutative Formulas and Frege Lower Bounds*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2015.412.

bib.title: Deterministic PIT for general noncommutative circuits

title: BPP equals P
open: Determine whether every bounded-error randomized polynomial-time algorithm can be replaced by a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm.
status: Open for decades. Strong circuit-hardness assumptions imply derandomization, but the required unconditional hardness is missing.
why: Determines whether randomness provides an inherent polynomial-time computational advantage.
key_works: Nisan and Wigderson (1994), *Hardness vs Randomness*; Impagliazzo and Wigderson (1997), *P = BPP if E Requires Exponential Circuits*; Impagliazzo (2003), arXiv:cs/0304040.

title: BPL equals L
open: Derandomize bounded-error logarithmic-space computation while retaining \(O(\log n)\) workspace.
status: Open for decades. General space-bounded generators and simulations incur additional space; recent work sharpens equivalences between logspace derandomization and hardness.
why: Would make randomized streaming-style computations deterministic without increasing their memory order.
key_works: Nisan (1992), *Pseudorandom Generators for Space-Bounded Computation*; Shalunov (2024), *Leakage-Resilient Hardness Equivalence to Logspace Derandomization*, arXiv:2312.14023, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2024.83.

title: Optimal-seed generators for general branching programs
open: Construct an explicit generator with \(O(\log n)\) seed length fooling polynomial-length, polynomial-width read-once branching programs to inverse-polynomial error.
status: A longstanding target beyond currently available general seed-length bounds. Merely proving BPL = L would not automatically provide this particular black-box generator.
why: Supplies reusable, randomness-efficient simulation rather than problem-specific derandomization.
key_works: Nisan (1992); Tal (2020), *Derandomizing Space-Bounded Computation* workshop materials; Shalunov (2024).

bib.title: Optimal-seed generators for general branching programs

title: Does derandomizing PromiseZPP derandomize PromiseBPP?
open: Prove or refute the implication \(\mathrm{PromiseZPP}\subseteq\mathrm P \Rightarrow \mathrm{PromiseBPP}\subseteq\mathrm P\).
status: Explicitly retained as an open problem in the 2024 Luca Trevisan memorial collection. Known relationships between zero-error and bounded-error randomness do not settle this implication for promise problems.
why: Identifies whether eliminating one form of randomness is already sufficient to eliminate another.
key_works: Fortnow, Goldreich, Håstad, Vadhan, and Williamson (2024), open-problem contributions in the Luca Trevisan memorial collection.

title: Near-linear seed length in generic OWF-to-PRG constructions
open: Starting from an arbitrary one-way function on \(n\)-bit inputs, construct a secure pseudorandom generator with seed length \(n^{1+o(1)}\), under a clearly specified black-box security-preserving reduction.
status: Generic constructions incur substantial overhead; stronger results are available for special classes such as regular one-way functions. The unrestricted near-linear target remains open in the cited problem formulation.
why: Would make foundational cryptographic reductions quantitatively useful.
key_works: Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin, and Luby (1999), *A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function*; Trevisan memorial collection (2024).

bib.title: Near-linear seed length in generic OWF-to-PRG constructions

title: Near-linear oracle complexity in OWF-to-PRG constructions
open: Reduce the number of calls to an arbitrary one-way function in a generic PRG construction to \(n^{1+o(1)}\), with explicit security loss and input-length conventions.
status: This is a separate resource question from seed length. Known generic upper bounds and black-box lower bounds leave a substantial gap.
why: Oracle-call overhead controls the actual cost of turning a hardness primitive into pseudorandomness.
key_works: Håstad–Impagliazzo–Levin–Luby (1999); Goldreich’s contribution to the 2024 Trevisan memorial problems.

bib.title: Near-linear oracle complexity in OWF-to-PRG constructions

title: Two-source extraction at the optimal leading entropy constant
open: Construct a polynomial-time explicit one-bit extractor for two independent \(n\)-bit sources of min-entropy \(\log_2 n+O(1)\), with a fixed small error such as 0.01.
status: Li’s 2023 work achieved \(O(\log n)\) entropy. The unresolved target here is the optimal leading constant and additive gap, not merely logarithmic entropy.
why: Approaches the information-theoretic limit of extracting randomness from extremely weak independent sources.
key_works: Li (2023), *Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*, arXiv:2303.06802, DOI: 10.1109/FOCS57990.2023.00075.

bib.title: Two-source extraction at the optimal leading entropy constant

title: Strongly explicit optimal Ramsey graphs
open: Construct graphs on \(N\) vertices with neither clique nor independent set larger than \(O(\log N)\), with adjacency computable in time polynomial in \(\log N\).
status: Random graphs achieve the desired order. Explicit constructions remain weaker; Li’s 2023 extractor advances yield polylogarithmic Ramsey bounds, not the optimal logarithmic bound.
why: Would make probabilistic extremal-combinatorial behavior efficiently explicit.
key_works: Erdős (1947), probabilistic Ramsey lower bound; Li (2023), arXiv:2303.06802.

title: Optimal explicit restricted-isometry matrices
open: Deterministically construct \(m\times N\) matrices with fixed restricted-isometry constant, sparsity \(k\), and \(m=O(k\log(N/k))\), in polynomial time.
status: Random matrices achieve this order. Explicit constructions have broken some older barriers but do not match the general optimal tradeoff.
why: Would remove randomness and improve guarantees in compressed sensing and sparse recovery.
key_works: Bourgain et al. (2011), explicit RIP constructions; Mixon, *Explicit Matrices with the Restricted Isometry Property: Breaking the Square-Root Bottleneck*, arXiv:1403.3427.

title: Fourier entropy–influence conjecture
open: Prove that every Boolean function satisfies \(H(\widehat f^2)\le C\,\mathrm{Inf}(f)\) for a universal constant \(C\).
status: Proposed by Friedgut and Kalai in 1996. Many special classes are understood; the universal inequality remains open.
why: Would tightly connect spectral complexity, sensitivity to noise, and learnability.
key_works: Friedgut and Kalai (1996), conjecture; Kalai (2007), *The Entropy/Influence Conjecture*, author exposition.

title: Fourier min-entropy–influence conjecture
open: Prove \(-\log_2\max_S \widehat f(S)^2\le C\,\mathrm{Inf}(f)\) for every Boolean function and a universal \(C\).
status: A weaker but still unresolved relative of FEI. Recent work improves necessary lower bounds on the constant rather than establishing the general inequality.
why: Would guarantee a substantial Fourier coefficient whenever total influence is small.
key_works: *A Lower Bound on the Constant in the Fourier Min-Entropy/Influence Conjecture* (2025), DOI: 10.1016/j.dam.2024.12.011; authors (verify).

title: Mansour’s conjecture
open: Prove that an \(s\)-term DNF has nearly all Fourier mass on a set of polynomially many coefficients for every fixed approximation error.
status: Proposed in the early 1990s. Random-DNF and restricted-parameter cases are known; the general concentration statement remains unresolved.
why: Would substantially improve understanding of the spectral and learning complexity of DNF.
key_works: Mansour’s original Fourier-learning work; *Mansour’s Conjecture Is True for Random DNF Formulas* (2010), ECCC TR10-023; *Sharper Bounds on Fourier Concentration of DNFs*, arXiv:2109.04525.

title: Superpolynomial Frege lower bounds
open: Exhibit an explicit family of propositional tautologies requiring superpolynomial-size Frege proofs.
status: Open since modern proof complexity began. Strong lower bounds for resolution and bounded-depth systems have not extended to unrestricted Frege.
why: Would establish inherent limitations of a central model of ordinary propositional reasoning.
key_works: Cook and Reckhow (1979); Li, Tzameret, and Wang (2015), *Non-Commutative Formulas and Frege Lower Bounds*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2015.412.

title: Superpolynomial Extended Frege lower bounds
open: Prove superpolynomial proof-size lower bounds for Extended Frege, which permits naming intermediate formulas.
status: Open for decades and stronger than the corresponding Frege target. Recent work explores implications of such lower bounds for computational hardness.
why: Would limit a proof system capable of efficiently expressing circuit-style reasoning.
key_works: Pich and Santhanam, *Towards P ≠ NP from Extended Frege Lower Bounds*, ECCC TR23-199; journal DOI: 10.1145/3801091.

title: Superpolynomial AC⁰[p]-Frege lower bounds
open: Find explicit tautologies requiring superpolynomial-size bounded-depth Frege proofs when modular-counting connectives are allowed.
status: Ordinary bounded-depth Frege has strong lower bounds; modular extensions remain substantially harder.
why: Tests whether algebraic counting enables fundamentally shorter proofs of combinatorial principles.
key_works: Razborov–Smolensky modular-circuit techniques; Krajíček (2019), *Proof Complexity*; Li–Tzameret–Wang (2015).

title: Ideal Proof System lower bounds
open: Prove superpolynomial arithmetic-circuit lower bounds on Ideal Proof System certificates for an explicit family of unsatisfiable polynomial systems.
status: Introduced in 2014. General lower bounds are tightly linked to major arithmetic circuit lower bounds, explaining both the promise and difficulty.
why: Could unify algebraic complexity and proof complexity in a common lower-bound program.
key_works: Grochow and Pitassi, *The Ideal Proof System: Circuit Complexity, Proof Complexity, and PIT*, DOI: 10.1145/3230742.

s2_matches.title: Lower Bounds against the Ideal Proof System in Finite Fields

title: Existence of a p-optimal propositional proof system
open: Determine whether a Cook–Reckhow proof system for TAUT exists that polynomially simulates every other such system.
status: Open for decades. Oracle constructions reveal independence among related optimality and completeness conjectures but do not decide the unrelativized question.
why: Asks whether there can be a universally efficient framework for propositional proofs.
key_works: Cook and Reckhow (1979); Dose (2019), DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2019.47.

bib.title: Existence of a p-optimal propositional proof system

title: Unconditional NP-hardness of total MCSP
open: Prove that the Minimum Circuit Size Problem for complete truth tables is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions.
status: Open since the 1950s–1970s origins of circuit minimization. Partial-function MCSP and conditional hardness results do not settle total MCSP under this reduction.
why: Would explain the apparent intractability of recognizing computational structure in explicit data.
key_works: Hirahara (2022), partial-MCSP hardness; Hirahara and Ilango (2025), *NP-Hardness of the Minimum Circuit Size Problem from Well-Studied Assumptions*, DOI: 10.1109/FOCS63196.2025.00087.

title: NP-hardness of total minimum formula size
open: Prove unconditional NP-hardness of deciding whether a complete truth table has a Boolean formula of size at most a supplied bound.
status: Strong conditional hardness is known, including ETH-based results. The standard unconditional NP-hardness question remains separate.
why: Clarifies the computational cost of optimal symbolic-expression compression.
key_works: Ilango, *The Minimum Formula Size Problem Is (ETH) Hard*; Hirahara and Ilango (2023), *NP-Hardness of Approximating Meta-Complexity*, DOI: 10.1145/3564246.3585154.

bib.title: NP-hardness of total minimum formula size

title: Strong bounded-depth Frege bounds for random 3-CNF
open: Prove superpolynomial, ideally exponential, bounded-depth Frege refutation-size lower bounds for random unsatisfiable 3-CNF formulas with a sufficiently large constant clause-to-variable ratio.
status: A 2024 result obtains \(n^{1+\varepsilon_d}\)-type bounds for fixed proof depth \(d\). The stronger growth targets remain unresolved.
why: Would connect proof complexity to experimentally hard random satisfiability instances.
key_works: Gryaznov and Talebanfard (2024), *Bounded-Depth Frege Lower Bounds for Random 3-CNFs via Deterministic Restrictions*, arXiv:2403.02275.

bib.title: Strong bounded-depth Frege bounds for random 3-CNF

title: Does Frege polynomially simulate Extended Frege?
open: Determine whether extension variables can always be eliminated from Extended Frege proofs with only polynomial growth and polynomial-time translation.
status: Open for decades. This compares proof-system strength directly and is not identical to proving lower bounds for either system.
why: Determines whether introducing names for intermediate propositions creates a superpolynomial proof advantage.
key_works: Cook and Reckhow (1979); Krajíček (2019), *Proof Complexity*; Pich–Santhanam’s Extended Frege work.

bib.title: Does Frege polynomially simulate Extended Frege?

title: Exponential Time Hypothesis
open: Prove or refute that 3-SAT on \(n\) variables cannot be solved in \(2^{o(n)}\) time.
status: Formulated around 1999–2001. Exact algorithms improve exponential bases, but no subexponential algorithm or unconditional exponential lower bound is known.
why: Supports quantitative lower bounds far more precise than NP-hardness.
key_works: Impagliazzo, Paturi, and Zane (2001), *Which Problems Have Strongly Exponential Complexity?*, DOI: 10.1006/jcss.2001.1774.

s2_matches.title: The Quantum Strong Exponential-Time Hypothesis

title: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis
open: Determine whether, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some clause width \(k\) makes \(k\)-SAT unsolvable in \(O((2-\varepsilon)^n)\) time.
status: Open since Impagliazzo–Paturi’s work. Refuting SETH would not necessarily refute ETH.
why: Anchors sharp running-time barriers for many polynomial-time and exponential-time problems.
key_works: Impagliazzo and Paturi (2001), *On the Complexity of k-SAT*; Vassilevska Williams (2018), *Some Open Problems in Fine-Grained Complexity*, DOI: 10.1145/3300150.3300158.

s2_matches.title: 2 ( Strong ) Exponential Time Hypothesis

title: Nondeterministic SETH
open: Determine whether certifying unsatisfiability of sufficiently wide CNF formulas still requires essentially \(2^n\) nondeterministic time.
status: Introduced to study limits of fine-grained reductions. It is stronger in a different direction than ordinary deterministic SETH.
why: Explains why some desired reductions would themselves imply unexpected algorithmic breakthroughs.
key_works: Carmosino, Gao, Impagliazzo, Mihajlin, Paturi, and Schneider (2016), *Nondeterministic Extensions of the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis and Consequences for Non-Reducibility*.

title: Gap Exponential Time Hypothesis
open: Prove or refute exponential-time hardness of distinguishing satisfiable 3-CNF from formulas in which every assignment violates a fixed positive fraction of clauses.
status: A central hypothesis in approximation and parameterized hardness. Ordinary ETH does not currently imply the standard Gap-ETH formulation.
why: Supplies robust hardness that survives approximation-preserving transformations.
key_works: Dinur’s and Manurangsi–Raghavendra’s 2016 Gap-ETH formulations; Vassilevska Williams’s fine-grained survey.

title: Counting SETH
open: Determine whether counting satisfying assignments to sufficiently wide CNF formulas requires \(2^{(1-o(1))n}\) time.
status: A longstanding counting analogue of SETH. Decision algorithms and counting algorithms need not have the same optimal exponential rate.
why: Underlies fine-grained lower bounds for exact counting, partition functions, and enumeration.
key_works: Impagliazzo–Paturi–Zane (2001); Dell et al., *Exponential Time Complexity of the Permanent and the Tutte Polynomial* (2014).

title: Truly subquadratic 3SUM
open: Give an \(O(n^{2-\varepsilon})\)-time algorithm for 3SUM for some fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) in the standard real-RAM model, or establish an appropriate conditional barrier.
status: Quadratic time has been improved by subpolynomial factors, but a fixed exponent improvement remains unknown.
why: Controls conjectured lower bounds for numerous geometric problems.
key_works: Gajentaan and Overmars (1995), *On a Class of O(n²) Problems in Computational Geometry*; Grønlund and Pettie (2014), *Threesomes, Degenerates, and Love Triangles*.

title: Truly subcubic weighted APSP
open: Compute all-pairs shortest paths in arbitrary weighted directed graphs in \(O(n^{3-\varepsilon})\) time for a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), under standard weight and arithmetic conventions.
status: Subcubic-by-subpolynomial-factor algorithms are known. A fixed exponent improvement remains a central open problem.
why: Would improve a large equivalence class of path, matrix, and optimization problems.
key_works: Vassilevska Williams and Williams (2018), *Subcubic Equivalences Between Path, Matrix, and Triangle Problems*, DOI: 10.1145/3186893.

title: Truly subquadratic min-plus convolution
open: Compute \(c_k=\min_{i+j=k}(a_i+b_j)\) for two arbitrary length-\(n\) sequences in \(O(n^{2-\varepsilon})\) time.
status: Open despite faster algorithms for restricted inputs and numerous equivalence reductions.
why: Would accelerate knapsack-like dynamic programs and many optimization recurrences.
key_works: Cygan, Mucha, Węgrzycki, and Włodarczyk (2017), *On Problems Equivalent to (min,+)-Convolution*; Vassilevska Williams’s survey.

title: Orthogonal Vectors Hypothesis
open: Settle whether, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), some constant \(c\) makes orthogonal-pair detection among \(n\) Boolean vectors of dimension \(c\log n\) require \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) time.
status: Implied by standard SETH formulations, but not independently established. Low-dimensional variants have faster algorithms.
why: Provides a widely reusable hardness source for similarity search and sequence problems.
key_works: Williams (2005), *A New Algorithm for Optimal 2-Constraint Satisfaction and Its Implications*; Vassilevska Williams (2018).

title: Online Matrix–Vector Multiplication conjecture
open: Determine whether processing \(n\) online Boolean matrix–vector products against a fixed \(n\times n\) matrix requires \(n^{3-o(1)}\) total time, with the preprocessing convention explicitly fixed.
status: Proposed in 2015; a major foundation of dynamic lower bounds. Each answer must precede the next vector.
why: Captures the cost of online dependence that offline matrix multiplication can avoid.
key_works: Henzinger, Krinninger, Nanongkai, and Saranurak (2015), *Unifying and Strengthening Hardness for Dynamic Problems via the Online Matrix-Vector Multiplication Conjecture*, arXiv:1504.06148.

title: Optimal exponent for fixed-size clique detection
open: For fixed \(k\) divisible by three, determine whether \(k\)-clique detection can beat the matrix-multiplication-based exponent \(\omega k/3\) by a fixed positive amount.
status: Matrix multiplication supplies the standard general benchmark. Its optimality is conjectural and should not be confused with NP-hardness when \(k\) is part of the input.
why: Would sharpen fine-grained complexity of dense subgraph detection.
key_works: Nešetřil and Poljak (1985), *On the Complexity of the Subgraph Problem*; Vassilevska Williams (2018).

title: Derive 3SUM hardness from SETH
open: Construct a fine-grained reduction showing that a truly subquadratic 3SUM algorithm would refute SETH, or prove a precisely stated barrier to such reductions.
status: The main fine-grained conjectures remain incompletely connected. Existing nondeterministic barriers constrain particular reduction strategies, not every conceivable proof.
why: Would reduce the number of independent assumptions needed for geometric lower bounds.
key_works: Carmosino et al. (2016), nondeterministic SETH and non-reducibility; Vassilevska Williams (2018).

title: Derive APSP hardness from SETH
open: Show that a truly subcubic general weighted APSP algorithm would yield a fixed-base improvement for sufficiently wide SAT, or establish a rigorous limitation of a specified reduction framework.
status: Still a major missing connection among fine-grained hypotheses.
why: Would unify many conditional lower bounds now resting on different assumptions.
key_works: Vassilevska Williams and Williams (2018), DOI: 10.1145/3186893; Carmosino et al. (2016).

title: Log-rank conjecture
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Prove that deterministic two-party communication complexity is bounded by a polynomial in the logarithm of the real rank of the communication matrix.
status: Open since the late 1970s–1980s. Bounds depending approximately on the square root of rank remain far from polynomial dependence on log-rank; new equivalent formulations appeared in 2025–2026.
why: Would connect algebraic simplicity to efficient distributed communication.
key_works: Lovász and Saks (1988); Hambardzumyan, Lovett, and Shirley, *The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations*, arXiv:2510.02583, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2026.7.

title: Existence of a dynamically optimal online binary search tree
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Construct an online BST whose cost on every access sequence is within a constant factor of the best offline BST execution, allowing the standard additive initialization term.
status: Open since the 1980s. Tango trees achieve \(O(\log\log n)\)-competitiveness, but constant competitiveness remains unknown.
why: Would establish a universally adaptive comparison-search structure.
key_works: Sleator and Tarjan (1985), *Self-Adjusting Binary Search Trees*; Demaine, Harmon, Iacono, and Pătraşcu (2007), *Dynamic Optimality—Almost*.

title: Dynamic optimality of splay trees
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Prove that the splay-tree algorithm is constant-competitive with the offline optimal BST.
status: Conjectured in 1985. A July 2026 preprint reports \(O(\log\log n(\log\log\log n)^2)\)-competitiveness, a major advance but not constant competitiveness.
why: Would justify a particularly simple, widely studied self-adjusting structure as universally optimal.
key_works: Sleator and Tarjan (1985), DOI: 10.1145/3828.3835; Chmel et al. (2026), *Splay Trees Are Almost Dynamically Optimal*, arXiv:2607.18498.

title: Dynamic optimality of Greedy BST
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Prove constant competitiveness of the online Greedy BST algorithm against the offline optimum.
status: Long conjectured. Guo, Pettie, Skora, and Wan’s August 2026 preprint reports competitiveness \(2^{O(\sqrt{\log\log n})}\), not a constant.
why: Would validate a geometrically motivated alternative route to optimal adaptive search.
key_works: Lucas and Munro’s greedy-BST proposals; Guo et al. (2026), *The Greedy Binary Search Tree Is Non-trivially Competitive*, arXiv:2608.04410.

title: Splay-tree deque conjecture
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Prove that any sequence of deque operations implemented using splay trees takes linear total time, up to initialization.
status: Open since the 1980s. Very slowly growing overhead bounds are known, but the exact linear target remains unresolved.
why: Tests whether splaying automatically attains optimal performance for a basic restricted access discipline.
key_works: Tarjan’s deque conjecture; Pettie (2008), *Splay Trees, Davenport–Schinzel Sequences, and the Deque Conjecture*.

title: Splay-tree traversal conjecture
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Prove that accessing the preorder traversal of one BST in an arbitrary initial splay tree takes \(O(n)\) total time.
status: Open since Sleator–Tarjan’s original work. Known access theorems do not establish the full conjecture.
why: Would show that splay trees recover hidden tree structure with optimal overhead.
key_works: Sleator and Tarjan (1985), *Self-Adjusting Binary Search Trees*, DOI: 10.1145/3828.3835; Chmel et al. (2026), arXiv:2607.18498.

title: Linear-time integer sorting for unrestricted word length
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Sort \(n\) word-sized integers in \(O(n)\) time on a standard word RAM for arbitrary word length \(w\ge\log n\), without charging unbounded-cost operations.
status: Decades old. The case \(w=O(\log n)\) admits radix-based linear sorting; the unrestricted-word target is different and unresolved.
why: Would close the gap between comparison sorting and the apparent power of integer operations.
key_works: Han and Thorup (2002), *Integer Sorting in O(n√log log n) Expected Time and Linear Space*; Han (2004), *Deterministic Sorting in O(n log log n) Time and Linear Space*.

title: Dynamically optimal external-memory search trees
subfield: Communication complexity and adaptive data structures
open: Develop a constant-competitive online B-tree or external-memory search structure relative to a precisely defined offline block-access and restructuring model.
status: Existing models and Belga B-tree results provide nonconstant competitive guarantees. Both the optimal algorithm and the most useful comparison model remain active questions.
why: Extends adaptivity guarantees to databases and storage systems, where block transfers dominate cost.
key_works: Demaine, Iacono, Koumoutsos, and Langerman, Belga B-tree work; *What Does Dynamic Optimality Mean in External Memory?*

title: FPT versus W[1]
subfield: Parameterized algorithms, kernelization, and structural graph algorithms
open: Prove or refute that parameterized Clique admits an \(f(k)n^{O(1)}\)-time algorithm.

title: EFX plus Pareto optimality for personalized bi-valued goods
open: Determine whether every additive-goods instance in which each agent has its own two positive utility levels admits an allocation that is both EFX and Pareto optimal.
status: A restricted but unresolved efficiency–fairness compatibility problem. Negative 2026 results for bi-valued chores must not be transferred to goods.
why: Tests whether fairness can be achieved without avoidable welfare loss.

open: Determine the largest constant \(\alpha\) such that every additive-goods instance admits an allocation giving each agent at least \(\alpha\) times its maximin share, and determine whether that guarantee is efficiently achievable.
status: Exact MMS allocations need not exist. Successively improved positive guarantees leave a gap to the best impossibility examples.
why: Would identify the strongest universal version of a major fairness benchmark.

title: Can quantum computers solve all NP problems efficiently?

open: Determine whether \(\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}\).
status: No polynomial-time quantum algorithm for general NP-complete problems is known; black-box search lower bounds do not establish the desired unrelativized exclusion.
why: Defines the limits of quantum acceleration for combinatorial optimization.
key_works: Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard, and Vazirani (1997), *Strengths and Weaknesses of Quantum Computing*; Watrous (2008), arXiv:0804.3401.

title: QMA versus QCMA

open: Determine whether polynomial-size quantum witnesses provide more verification power than polynomial-size classical witnesses checked by a quantum verifier.
status: Oracle separations are known, but the unrelativized equality or separation remains open.
why: Clarifies whether quantum information itself is essential in efficiently verifiable certificates.

open: Determine whether two unentangled quantum witnesses yield more computational power than one quantum witness.
status: Constant numbers of unentangled witnesses can be reduced to two in important formulations, but equality with QMA remains open.
why: Tests the computational significance of an unentanglement promise.

title: Quantum PCP conjecture for local Hamiltonians
subfield: Quantum complexity and locally decodable codes
open: Prove QMA-hardness of approximating ground-state energy to a fixed positive fraction of the number of bounded-norm local terms.
status: Open since the 2000s. Results on nonlocal games, NLTS, and good quantum LDPC codes do not by themselves resolve this local-Hamiltonian formulation.
why: Would show that even coarse estimates of many-body ground energy can be quantum-computationally intractable.
